sequencing_note: This v0 is frozen AFTER both source pooled animal photo odds and external ERA5 522-day seasonal environment result were already inspected. Therefore it is a diagnostic exploratory alignment, never a confirmatory test or independently hidden replication.
question: Do source-admissible matched-photoperiod camera date pairs represent the same regional weather contrast as all astronomical candidate pairs? Across three calendar cycles, do yearly descriptive photo-time changes agree with a simplistic warmer-falling-branch heat-avoidance account?

environment_source.scope: ONE regional coarse public representative cell, not physical camera locations

Compute mean falling-minus-rising ERA5 regional T2m maximum and trailing 30-day precipitation difference across ACTUAL original eligible site×date pairs, with literal replication weighted by sites as descriptive observation support; do not treat pairs as independent climate samples.

For every original detected source taxon, output branch-zone source photo counts and site-stratified Mantel-Haenszel descriptive odds edge/core and night/day per cycle, undefined odds remain undefined, zeros retained.
Leave everything as descriptive, do not calculate inferential p values or a 3-year regression.

hard_limits: Source operational support is inferred only from first/last valid SD card photos, not true device on/off zone hours.
Site-specific detection q or independent true animal passages not known.
Climate single spatial cell and at most three cycles cannot estimate a population environmental slope or causal heat response.
Source site/date mirror weather and photo records are observational and do not establish endogenous photoperiod memory.
Previous pooled photo OR results remain frozen; no adjustment rescues or retroactively confirms them.
No exact source camera location, station ID, raw photo timestamp or per-station climate value in exported artifacts.
Year-cycles are NOT independent landscape replications and 24,290 pairs are not independent weather replicates.
